title: [Performance][0.32.0] Optimize KDA RecoverSSM aligned state commit
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Cherry-pick #20474 onto `releases/v0.32.0rc`: optimize GLM KDA RecoverSSM aligned state commit with separate boundary/non-boundary routing and A5 grouped-head support. Include the serving-documentation cleanup.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Lower commit latency without new serving options or cache-layout changes. Small or boundary-heavy workloads can regress; see the referenced measurements.

### How was this patch tested?

Validated this head with **vLLM v0.32.0** (`5df63a7203cdb9328d824a27b682e77c7b9928be`). A3/A5 each passed 212 tests and 1,552 independent FP64 operator-output comparisons, plus 60 same-runtime operator A/B cases.

Whole-model ReplaySSM OFF/ON comparisons use prefix caching, target/MTP graphs and true C90 decode. Each arm includes full 1,319-question GSM8K evaluation; all 48 CPU/NPU traces were checked. [Detailed results, acceptance, accuracy deltas, regressions and compilation audit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20524#issuecomment-6554091747).
